headline: US stocks extended three-day slide as oil topped $101 and Treasury yields hit 2023 highs on US-Iran tensions and Treasury buyback disappointment ahead of PPI, OPEC report and ECB decision
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 (SPX) fell 0.48% to 7,636.36, the Dow (DJI) dropped 0.77% to 52,380.66, and the Nasdaq (COMP) slid 0.64% to 26,253.34, with the S&P posting its largest three-day point and percentage decline since July 20 and ending about 2% below its August 13 record high.
- Brent crude (@QA) rose more than 3% to settle above $101 per barrel after escalated US-Iran tensions disrupted Strait of Hormuz shipping and included the US disabling 10 Iranian tankers.
- A smaller-than-hoped $6 billion longer-term Treasury buyback from the US Treasury disappointed traders and pushed the 10-year yield to its highest level since 2023.
- Energy was the only S&P 500 (SPX) sector to rise, gaining roughly 1.1% on strength in Exxon Mobil (XOM), Chevron (CVX) and APA (APA).
- Industrials lagged with a decline of around 1.5%, while consumer discretionary weakness included Vertiv (VRT), which sank nearly 10%.
- Meta Platforms (META) climbed about 6.5% after unveiling its autonomous AI agent Muse.
- Cloudflare (NET) jumped more than 10% on a new security partnership with OpenAI (OAIW).
- Casey’s General Stores (CASY) fell nearly 15% despite an earnings beat, while Apple (AAPL) slipped 0.3% after new CEO John Ternus launched the first foldable iPhone Duo.
- In after-hours trading, Cooper Companies (COO) dropped about 16% on a revenue miss and American Eagle Outfitters (AEO) fell more than 10% after cutting its outlook.
- Traders looked ahead to Thursday’s US producer price index data, OPEC’s monthly report and an upcoming ECB policy decision.
